title: Shimabara Rebellion
summary: In 1637–1638 peasants and Christians on the Shimabara Peninsula and the Amakusa Islands rose against their lords and held Hara Castle against a shogunate army of more than 100,000. The castle fell in April 1638 and the sources report that nearly all of the roughly 37,000 participants were killed. The shogunate tightened its anti-Christian policy and restrictions on foreign trade.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on the start (October 1637, 11th month of 1637, or 17 December 1637) and on the end (a late-February 1638 date versus 15 April 1638). The range spans both.

importance.justification: A large uprising whose suppression is tied by the sources to the shogunate's anti-Christian and foreign-trade restrictions.

audience_note: Describes the reported massacre of tens of thousands of rebels, including women and children, after the fall of Hara Castle; no graphic detail is given.
